scope: Read-only primary Catholic source investigation for a separate old-style Julian Byzantine feast calendar in civil years 2026 and 2027; no source lectionary imported.
nativeReadingsRecommendation: Keep the separate old-style calendar's readings empty until its own dated Catholic appointments are verified. Do not shift the new-style UGCC or fully Gregorian Royal Doors readings by thirteen days.

sources.publisher: Ukrainian Greek Catholic Church; explanation by its Father and Head
sources.verification: Live published primary HTML read on 2026-10-03
confirms: The fixed feast cycle and Paschal cycle are separate.
Ukraine's reform moved all fixed feasts to the new style, retaining the existing Paschalion.
Historical old-style Nativity was celebrated on civil 7 January; the explanation contrasts it with 25 December.
Theophany, Nicholas, Protection and Exaltation must move with the same fixed calendar; Christmas alone cannot be changed.
bounds: Historical reform explanation, not an annual 2026/2027 appointment table.
The local permission discussed for Ukraine was time-limited to 2025; this does not establish the current discipline of every diaspora parish.
sources.rights: Page requests a source link when spreading its information; original third-party wording not relicensed.

sources.underlyingCredit: Liudmyla Panasiuk, UP. Zhyttia; interview with Fr Roman Fihas, director of the Ukrainian Catholic University Institute of Ecumenical Studies
confirms: The 2023 fixed-feast reform moved dates thirteen days earlier while leaving the Eastern Paschal calculation.
The article explicitly gives Eastern Pascha as civil 12 April 2026.
bounds: Hosted primary church explanation with an underlying publication credit.
A computed Pascha date does not establish a complete daily lectionary.

generatorReview.method: Read-only function inspection plus offline independent civil-date comparisons. Every curated fixed month/day landing in 2026 or2027 was independently compared with Gregorian chronology plus the applicable thirteen-day offset. The generator uses Julian-day arithmetic, not that permanent offset.
checksPassed: Previous source year's Julian25December maps to civil7January in both2026 and2027.
All expected curated fixed dates are present within the correct civil year.
Theophany maps to civil19January in both years.
2026 old-style Annunciation joins Great and Holy Tuesday on7April.
Special Sundays are recomputed from converted fixed ranges, not copied by thirteen-day shifting of a Sunday table.
